summary: Inotuzumab ozogamicin (Besponsa) is a CD22-directed antibody-drug conjugate that delivers the cytotoxic calicheamicin derivative N-acetyl-gamma-calicheamicin into CD22-positive B-lymphoblasts. It is indicated for adults and pediatric patients (1 year and older) with relapsed or refractory CD22-positive B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). It carries a BOXED WARNING for hepatotoxicity, including fatal and life-threatening hepatic veno-occlusive disease (VOD), also called sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (SOS), and for an increased risk of post-hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) non-relapse mortality. Dosing is given over a 21- to 28-day cycle with response-based adjustments.

Reconstitute each 0.9 mg vial with 4 mL Sterile Water for Injection to give 0.25 mg/mL; swirl gently, do not shake
Dilute the reconstituted solution in 0.9% sodium chloride to a final concentration of 0.01 to 0.1 mg/mL

Protect from light during reconstitution, dilution, and administration; complete administration within 8 hours of reconstitution

moa: Inotuzumab ozogamicin is a CD22-directed antibody-drug conjugate consisting of a humanized anti-CD22 monoclonal antibody covalently linked to N-acetyl-gamma-calicheamicin dimethylhydrazide, a cytotoxic calicheamicin derivative. After binding CD22 on the surface of B-lymphoblasts, the conjugate is internalized; the released calicheamicin derivative binds the minor groove of DNA and induces double-strand DNA breaks, leading to cell-cycle arrest and apoptotic cell death.

preg: Based on its mechanism and animal findings, inotuzumab ozogamicin can cause embryo-fetal harm. Verify pregnancy status before initiation; advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 8 months after the last dose, and males with female partners to use contraception for at least 5 months after the last dose.
lact: There are no data on the presence of the drug in human milk or its effects on the breastfed child. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for at least 2 months after the final dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is necessary in patients with mild to moderate renal impairment (CrCl 30-89 mL/min). It has not been studied in patients with severe renal impairment or end-stage renal disease.
hepatic: BOXED WARNING for hepatotoxicity, including fatal and life-threatening hepatic veno-occlusive disease (VOD/sinusoidal obstruction syndrome). Monitor liver tests (total bilirubin, AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase) before each dose and for signs of VOD. Interrupt dosing, reduce the dose, or permanently discontinue based on bilirubin and transaminase elevations; permanently discontinue if VOD/SOS occurs. Risk is higher with subsequent HSCT, conditioning regimens with 2 alkylating agents, and elevated pre-HSCT bilirubin.

major: QT-prolonging drugs (e.g., antiarrhythmics, certain antipsychotics, fluoroquinolones, azoles) - additive risk of QTc prolongation and arrhythmia
moderate: Other hepatotoxic agents - additive hepatic injury and VOD risk
minor: Live vaccines - reduced response and infection risk during immunosuppression
interactions.alcohol: No direct interaction; avoid alcohol given the risk of hepatotoxicity.
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate bilirubin, transaminases, and alkaline phosphatase, and reduce neutrophil, platelet, and hemoglobin levels; can prolong the QTc interval.

Torsades de pointes from QT prolongation

Limit treatment to 2 cycles before HSCT and avoid conditioning regimens with 2 alkylating agents to reduce VOD risk

missed: Doses are administered by a healthcare professional on a fixed schedule (Days 1, 8, 15). If a dose is missed or delayed, it is rescheduled by the treating team, maintaining a minimum interval of 6 days between doses within a cycle; do not double doses.
overdose: There is no known antidote. Overdose may worsen myelosuppression, hepatotoxicity (including VOD), and infusion-related reactions. Manage supportively with blood product support, treatment of infection and bleeding, intensive hepatic monitoring, and management of VOD; the conjugate is not removed by dialysis.
